blocks.text: # Proofpress Provenance Continuity Evaluation
## Review status

This directory records immutable transport-history slices and the accepted single-agent continuity follow-up. New formal work uses `openai/gpt-5.6-luna` for execution and `openai/gpt-5.6-terra` for blind scoring. Historic Harvey PSA, OpenRouter/Novita, and multi-agent artifacts remain auditable history only and are not resumed or pooled.

This `proofpress-dev` checkout is the canonical maintenance root for the study. `/Users/richardtang/Documents/Proofpress` is not a second source of truth and should not receive further research or documentation updates.
## The research question

Under the same task and budget, does a verified Proofpress continuity artifact help one agent in a fresh session recover the current justified decision better than an equal-sized ordinary memory note?

The study is deliberately not a claim that more context or more agents are better. It compares a continuous baseline, ordinary memory, and verified provenance; no future formal slice adds agents, roles, or raw-history conditions.
## Scope and comparison

The execution runtime is [Harvey LAB](https://github.com/harveyai/harvey-labs) v1.0's own task and scoring harness. Harvey tasks are not inherently agent-to-agent handoff tasks; our wrapper creates the controlled long-horizon workflow. One orchestrator role (in fresh planning and review sessions) coordinates evidence, decision-register, and drafting stages. Each completed stage emits a real work artifact, producing `V0 → V1 → V2 → V3 → V4` rather than one artificial two-agent transfer.
The active formal conditions are:

- `baseline_continuous`: one continuous session with no handoff artifact.
- `ordinary_memory`: the same agent resumes in a fresh session with an ordinary continuity note.
- `proofpress_provenance`: the same fresh-session flow with a verified native Proofpress continuity artifact.

The primary causal contrast is `proofpress_provenance − ordinary_memory`; `ordinary_memory − baseline_continuous` is only the session-restart reference. The route is MemConflict mechanism gate, C&H qualification slice, then APEX external-validity slice.
## What is here today

- `docs/RESEARCH_PLAN.md` — accepted follow-up protocol, observed Gate 1 boundary, arms, metrics, and gates.
- `docs/ARCHITECTURE.md` — the fixed centralized workflow and the treatment boundary.
- `docs/EXECUTION_PLAN.md` — staged implementation and run plan, including explicit stopping gates.
- `docs/RESULTS_MATRIX.md` — the three result matrices and how to interpret them.
- `docs/RUNBOOK.md` — operational prerequisites and what is or is not implemented today.
- `docs/ARA_PROOFPRESS.md` — ARA as research-management layer; Proofpress as independently verifiable artifact lineage.
- `ara/` — an Agent-Native Research Artifact for this study. It contains hypotheses and decisions, not invented results.
- `configs/gate-native-v1.draft.yaml` — a historical three-arm MAS draft, not the active Gateway contract.
- `pp_eval/`, `suites/`, and `tests/` — the pre-existing lightweight mechanism runtime. It is retained for smoke tests and does not yet claim to execute the official Harvey harness treatment wrapper.
## ARA installation

The official ARA source has been cloned at `third_party/ara-source` and its six local Codex skills were installed under `.codex/skills/`. Both locations are ignored by Git; their source URL, commit, installation command, and role are recorded in [ara/UPSTREAM.md](ara/UPSTREAM.md). ARA is the research-management layer only. Benchmark agents never receive its files, skills, or prompts.
## Phase 1 status

The internal MemConflict mechanism gate is complete: 12 frozen reversal cases × 2 attempts × 3 conditions = 72 local Codex runs. Gate A passed, Gate B failed. Proofpress matched ordinary memory on trusted success (83.3%), reduced stale/regression errors from 12.5% to 4.2%, but had lower task success (87.5% versus 95.8%). This is a bounded mechanism signal, not evidence of a task-quality gain. The sanitized record is in [evidence/phase1-memconflict-v1](evidence/phase1-memconflict-v1/README.md).

The Phase 1 runner recorded a requested model but not resolved provider, Gateway cost, or fallback telemetry. It is therefore not eligible for the formal Gateway matrix. Do not rerun it as if it were missing data; fix the telemetry boundary and independently qualify the next benchmark slice.
## Before any new model run

The completed Harvey Gate 1a/1b records are retained as evidence about an **external transport prototype** only. The accepted route is now MemConflict mechanism gate → C&H adapter/cost gate → APEX external-validity slice. The next model run must use the frozen Gateway contract and record requested/resolved model, actual provider, Gateway-reported `usage.cost`, token/latency values, and fallback status/metadata. A missing field is audit-visible but disqualifies that workflow from the formal matrix; local `$0` is never a cost substitute. Harvey, STATE-Bench, and later evidence/research benchmarks remain separate slices and are never pooled with Phase 1.
## Existing lightweight smoke runtime
The existing `pp-eval` commands still work for local fixture validation:

```bash
export PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME=/Users/richardtang/.cache/proofpress-eval
cd /Users/richardtang/proofpress-dev/experiments/provenance_handoff
uv sync --frozen
uv run pp-eval doctor --suite smoke-v1 --data-home "$PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME"
uv run pp-eval build --suite smoke-v1 --data-home "$PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME"
uv run pp-eval run --suite memconflict-v1 --data-home "$PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME" --arms baseline_continuous,ordinary_memory,proofpress_provenance --runner codex --model gpt-5.6-luna --attempts 2 --concurrency 1
uv run pp-eval grade --suite smoke-v1 --data-home "$PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME"
uv run pp-eval report --suite smoke-v1 --data-home "$PROOFPRESS_EVAL_HOME"
```
Those fixtures validate package construction, isolation, recording, and reports only. They are not a substitute for the Harvey-first study described in `docs/`.
